target_defect: The right countertop's surface variation is too faint and sparse, appearing mostly flat with short straight marks instead of the reference's broad, flowing pale-gray streaks.

observations.claim: The reference countertop has visible, softly varying elongated gray-white streaks over much of its surface; the reconstruction is predominantly near-white with a few faint straight marks.
observations.evidence: Direct comparison of the supplied reference and current reconstruction images, focusing on the right countertop. Differences in framing and lighting limit a pixel-for-pixel comparison.

observations.claim: The saved countertop uses a plain stone material and separate straight vein objects.
observations.evidence: build.py:6-8 defines the constant Principled material 'white stone'; build.py:34-40 assigns it to 'right marble counter' and creates straight rod objects named 'marble vein'. scene_state.json:7135-7170 records the counter and material, and :7241 onward records vein meshes.

observations.claim: The recorded trajectory changed camera and lighting after an initial render, but does not show a separate countertop texture experiment.
observations.evidence: sdk_events.json events 2, 3, 6, 8 and 9: the initial script creates the countertop and rods, followed by renders and a camera/light adjustment. objective_evidence.json:17-24 independently flags countertop surface variation as differing.

technical_hypotheses.hypothesis: A constant base color plus isolated straight rods may be unable to reproduce the broad, continuous variation seen in the reference.
technical_hypotheses.supporting_evidence: build.py:6-8 and 36-40 describe a uniform material and discrete straight rod veins; the current image shows mostly flat white with sparse marks.
technical_hypotheses.competing_explanation: The reference's streaks could partly be highlights or shading rather than inherent stone pattern; the images also have different framing.
technical_hypotheses.uncertainty: The reference material and underlying geometry are unknown, and the visual contribution of each mechanism is not isolated.

technical_hypotheses.hypothesis: Lighting, view transform, resolution or denoising may suppress the existing subtle vein contrast in the current render.
technical_hypotheses.supporting_evidence: build.py:77-86 specifies broad area lights, AgX, a 640 by 360 render and denoising; the rods and countertop use similar pale materials.
technical_hypotheses.competing_explanation: Even if more visible, the straight, separated rods may still lack the reference's broad flowing structure.
technical_hypotheses.uncertainty: No controlled render separating illumination and pattern contributions is recorded.

candidate_methods.method: Replace the discrete line appearance with a mapped procedural color pattern on a countertop-specific material, using warped, directional, softly blended variation.
candidate_methods.applicable_conditions: Useful if the broad streaks are best approximated as surface color variation and an editable, asset-free material is desired.
candidate_methods.verification: Render with camera and illumination held fixed; compare a countertop crop with the reference for continuity, direction, coverage and subtle contrast, including the visible edge.
candidate_methods.possible_side_effects: Repetition, excessive contrast, plastic-looking swirls or stretching at edges; changing a shared material could affect other objects.

candidate_methods.method: Test a curated or hand-painted image texture mapped to the counter, instead of procedural patterning; compare against a controlled lighting and roughness-only candidate.
candidate_methods.applicable_conditions: Useful when art-directed streak shapes are important, or when highlights rather than pigment may explain much of the variation.
candidate_methods.verification: Render each candidate under the same camera and lighting and compare counter crops; inspect a second light direction to distinguish fixed color marks from moving highlights.
candidate_methods.possible_side_effects: Image mapping can stretch or repeat and needs an appropriate licensed asset; roughness or lighting changes can alter neighboring surfaces and overall brightness.

error_hint: The right countertop reads as almost uniform white with a few faint straight marks, whereas the reference shows broader, flowing pale-gray variation across its surface.
strategy_extension: Test a countertop-specific mapped material that produces softly blended, elongated variation rather than relying on separate straight vein objects. Hold the camera and lighting fixed while comparing a countertop crop to the reference for the streaks' continuity, direction, coverage and contrast. Inspect the visible edge and neighboring surfaces as well so that improved patterning does not introduce stretching or unintended material changes.
exploration_extension: Implement and compare two candidates: a mapped procedural color pattern with gently warped directional variation, and an art-directed image texture with different streak shapes. Also test whether a roughness-and-lighting variation without added color pattern explains the reference better. Keep camera and render settings fixed for the main comparison, then use an alternate light direction to see which marks move as highlights. Compare countertop crops for streak continuity, coverage and contrast, and check the edge, neighboring materials, overall brightness and texture stretching for side effects.
knowledge_origin: Observable in the supplied images and natural trajectory: the visual mismatch, the named counter and rods, the plain material, and the camera/light adjustment. Procedural or image mapping, a roughness/lighting alternative, and controlled comparison renders are proposed technical priors, not established properties of the reference or previously tested solutions.
